title: Citadel Securities’ Rubner Says Stocks Are Set Up for Year-End Gains After Vote
detail:
Citadel Securities’ Rubner Says Stocks Are Set Up for Year-End Gains After Vote
Bloomberg · Source: Citadel Securities
Natalia Kniazhevich
Wed, November 4, 2026 at 10:14 AM MST 4 min read
^NDX

(Bloomberg) -- US stocks are primed for a year-end rebound as the midterm election removes a source of uncertainty, corporate earnings remain resilient and lackluster investor positioning leaves room for renewed buying, according to Citadel Securities' Scott Rubner.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Morgan Stanley Offers $2.3 Billion Debt for Dell Family Deal

Democrats Sweep to Control of Congress in Rebuke of Trump

What the Democrats' Sweep of Congress Means for Trump

Democrat El-Sayed Wins Michigan Race in Boost to Progressives

Democrats Clinch Huge Wins on Inflation Anger, Trump Fatigue

After a difficult October, investors had looked to the election as a potential catalyst for a recovery in equities. The technology-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index entered its third correction of the year on Monday, falling 10% from its early-October peak as concerns mounted over whether massive investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure will generate returns sufficient to justify elevated valuations.

Hedge funds have also cut exposure to US equities and increased bearish bets, pushing stock-market shorts close to a five-year high, while systematic investors have reduced their market exposure. For Rubner, this light positioning, combined with renewed corporate stock buybacks, persistent retail buying, and historically favorable post-midterm seasonality patterns, creates a compelling setup for US equities into year-end.

"With the election behind us and volatility potentially normalizing, there is considerable capacity for investors to rebuild risk," Rubner, the firm's head of equity and equity derivatives strategy, wrote in a note to clients Wednesday. "With uncertainty fading and several of the market's largest buyers returning, we believe the path of least resistance for U.S. equities is higher into year-end."

Already, stocks are "breathing a sigh of relief" after the elections, Rubner wrote, with all major indexes rallying Wednesday and the S&P 500 Index up 1.7% as of midday. Rubner sees several reasons for that trend to continue.

First, retail investors have already been net buyers of US equities for 22 consecutive sessions since Oct. 5, accumulating nearly $33 billion, according to Citadel Securities. The buying streak ranks as the sixth-longest and fifth-largest since 2017.

Purchases have averaged $1.5 billion per session, or 1.4 times the trailing-year average, even as the S&P 500 declined 2% over the period. Retail investors have also continued to buy market dips, increasing purchases by 7% on days when the S&P 500 fell while remaining roughly flat on advancing sessions.

The main US stock measures were pointing higher in Wednesday's premarket activity as traders parsed preliminary midterm election results that showed the Democratic Party securing control in both chambers of Congress.

The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.1% each before the opening bell, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 1.4%. The Nasdaq Composite and the S&P 500 finished Tuesday trading in the green, while the Dow closed lower.

The Democratic Party secured 54 seats in the 100-member Senate and 228 seats in the 435-member House of Representatives, ending Republican majorities in both chambers, preliminary election results by the Associated Press showed early Wednesday.

The AP had yet to call 2 Senate and 68 House races as of 7:30 am ET.

A Democratic Congress is likely to bring greater scrutiny on technology and artificial intelligence spending, Saxo Bank Investment and Options Strategist Koen Hoorelbeke said in a note.

Shares of SpaceX (SPCX), Tesla (TSLA) and CoreWeave (CRWV) were all down before the open, while healthcare stocks gained.

Treasury yields declined early Wednesday, with the two-year rate falling 0.8 basis points to 4.61% while the 10-year rate decreased 3.5 basis points to 4.92%.

Advanced Micro Devices' (AMD) shares advanced 1.2% pre-bell as the chip maker issued a stronger-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue outlook, while its results in the previous three-month period topped Wall Street estimates. Arista Networks (ANET) climbed 11% as the cloud computing firm posted robust third-quarter results.

McDonald's (MCD), Uber Technologies (UBER), CVS Health (CVS), Emerson Electric (EMR), Datadog (DDOG), Kraft Heinz (KHC), Performance Food (PFGC) and Wayfair (W) post their quarterly earnings before the bell, among others. Arm (ARM), Qualcomm (QCOM) and McKesson (MCK) release their results after the markets close.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil declined 0.8% to $95.28 a barrel, while Brent decreased 1.3% to $102.25 a barrel.

President Donald Trump told the Financial Times on Tuesday that the US has no immediate plans to strike Iran. A senior Iranian official told Reuters that the two countries remain far from a deal to end their war.

The ADP Employment report for October is scheduled to be released at 8:15 am ET. On Tuesday, official data showed job openings increased in September as all key metrics improved, with Oxford Economics calling labor market conditions "solid."

The Challenger Job Cut and the government's nonfarm payrolls data, both for October, are due on Thursday and Friday, respectively.

Wednesday's economic calendar also has the weekly mortgage applications bulletin at 7 am, followed by the international trade in goods and services report for September at 8:30 am. The purchasing managers' index composite final report from S&P Global (SPGI) for October is out at 9:45 am, followed by the Institute for Supply Management's services index for the same month at 10 am.

Spot gold gained 2.9% to $4,054 per troy ounce, while bitcoin increased 1.1% to $78,518.

Credit: Tom Brenner / Getty Images

Stock futures are pointing higher Wednesday morning after the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite logged gains on Tuesday; Shares of defense companies and contractors were sliding lower, among a number of notable movers in the wake of Election Day, as investors digested what a Democratic sweep may mean for economic policy, the construction of data centers and other issues; Shares of Advanced Micro Devices and Super Micro Computer were moving after the companies reported late Tuesday; and investors were gearing up for quarterly results from McDonald's and a number of other companies.

Here's what you need to know today.

Stock Futures Point Higher

Major stock indexes appear poised to rise as investors Wednesday morning filter through the midterm election results. Futures tied to the blue-chip Dow were recently up 1.8%, while those tied to the S&P 500 were up about 0.9%. Those associated with the Nasdaq 100 were up about 0.2%.

Oil prices were falling, with Brent crude—the global oil benchmark—down about 1.9% to $101.65 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate, the U.S. benchmark, was down about 1.5% to $94.67 a barrel. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield was at 4.92%, down from about 4.97% Tuesday night. Precious metals prices were climbing, as was bitcoin, which according to CoinDesk recently traded around $78,000.

Democrats Win Control of Congress

Voters had pocketbook issues on their mind, which fueled sweeping change in yesterday's Congressional elections. Democrats are poised to have majorities in the Senate and House of Representatives after flipping a number of districts in the midterm elections, according to The Associated Press. The party may try to reverse cuts to Medicaid and Medicare, rework trade policy and halt the war with Iran, which is driving up fuel prices. While the elections may have implications for economic policy, analysts say the partisan breakdown in D.C. hasn't historically had an impact on investors' portfolios.

At the state level, Democrats won five governorships previously held by Republicans, according to NBC News. New leadership may influence the construction of data centers, which are generally disliked by surrounding communities.

SpaceX, Tesla Shares, Defense Stocks Fall Post-Election

Investors were picking among stocks and sectors as they tried to size up post-election winners and losers. Defense company stocks fell as investors mulled what the election results may mean for the country's approach to conflict and international relations. Shares of Northrop Grumman (NOC) and Lockheed Martin (LMT) were recently down at least 3% on a morning where stocks appeared poised to climb. Companies that contract with the U.S. defense agencies were also off, with Palantir Technologies (PLTR) recently off by about 5% and Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX) down more than 7%. Tesla (TSLA) also fell, indicating that a much-expected merger with SpaceX could face more scrutiny.

US stock futures advanced on Wednesday as investors assessed the implications of Democratic gains in the midterm elections, while stronger-than-expected growth expectations from Advanced Micro Devices supported technology shares.

The election results indicated that Democrats had secured control of both chambers of Congress, raising questions about future US policy on artificial intelligence, trade and military operations in the Middle East.

Meanwhile, Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) shares surged more than 7% in after-hours trading after the semiconductor manufacturer forecast strong revenue growth for 2027, driven by demand for data centre processors.

Wall Street Futures Advance Ahead of Opening Bell

US equity futures moved higher during Wednesday's early trading session.

At 03:37 ET (08:37 GMT), S&P 500 futures had gained 15 points, or 0.2%, while Nasdaq 100 futures rose 64 points, also representing an increase of 0.2%.

Dow Jones Industrial Average futures advanced 237 points, or 0.5%.

The gains followed a mixed session on Wall Street, when the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite closed higher while the Dow Jones declined.

Investor sentiment had improved following signs of potential diplomatic progress in the conflict involving Iran, which helped reduce oil prices and supported equities.

However, uncertainty surrounding the Middle East and the sustainability of substantial AI infrastructure investment continued to influence market activity.

Recent US economic indicators also suggested resilient underlying conditions, with job openings reaching a four-month high and factory orders exceeding expectations.

Democrats Secure Congressional Majorities in US Midterm Elections

The Democratic Party secured majorities in both the House of Representatives and Senate following Tuesday's midterm elections, changing the political balance in Washington.

The results followed voter concerns over living costs, the conflict involving Iran and the economic implications of artificial intelligence.

Democratic gains extended into several areas traditionally supportive of President Donald Trump's Republican Party.

When the new Congress convenes in January, Democratic control of both chambers will give the party greater influence over legislation, government spending and congressional oversight.

However, President Trump will retain his constitutional veto power, meaning legislation approved by Congress could still be rejected by the White House.

AI Regulation Concerns Weigh on Technology Sentiment

Investors are assessing whether the new congressional balance could lead to stricter regulation of artificial intelligence and potentially slower investment in data centre infrastructure.
